overview.description: Derda is a two-player Jass game that was once popular in Poland, particularly among currency traders, gamblers, and the underworld during the communist era. It is closely related to Clobyosh and features unique bidding mechanics and bonus scoring for sequences and special cards.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Poland
Time Period: Peak popularity during communist era (1945-1989)
Historical Development: First played in Łódź and Warsaw, spread throughout Poland by 1960
Cultural Significance: Associated with cinkciarze (illicit currency traders), gamblers, and underworld figures; featured in the 1997 movie 'Sztos'
timeline: 1940s-1950s: Game emerges in Łódź and Warsaw, Poland
Communist era: Peak popularity among currency traders and gamblers
2020: Ryszard Zienkiewicz publishes book 'Derda' documenting the game
Present: Largely forgotten, maintained by handful of enthusiasts
history.evolution: Derda evolved from Jass game traditions and is closely related to Clobyosh. The game developed unique terminology and scoring systems reflective of its underground gambling culture.
history.cultural: Derda represents a fascinating piece of Polish gambling culture during the communist era. The game's jargon ('words' for bonuses) and association with currency trading provide insight into the period's underground economy.

rules.objective: Be first to achieve cumulative score of 500 points across multiple deals. Points scored for cards taken in tricks and bonuses ('words').
rules.gameplay:
1. First dealer chosen by drawing cards (higher card in trump order)
2. Deal 6 cards to each player, turn up 13th card for suggested trump
3. Bidding round 1: Non-dealer can 'play' suggested trump or 'pass'
4. If non-dealer passes, dealer can 'play', 'pass', or ask 'how many times?'
5. If both pass round 1, round 2 allows choosing different trump suit
6. Commercial offers can be made to throw in hand for points/deal advantage
7. Once trumps chosen, deal 3 more cards each
8. Player with 7 of trumps may exchange it for turn-up card
9. Non-dealer leads to first trick
10. Must follow suit if able; must play trump if cannot follow (if have trump)
11. Highest trump wins if trumps played; otherwise highest of led suit
12. Winner leads to next trick
keyRules: Trump Jack scores double: 2 points as jack + 20 as word = 22 total
Derda and 50 bonuses only scored by player with best sequence
Commercial offers allow throwing in hand for points/deal advantage
Must follow suit; if cannot follow, must play trump if held
7 of trumps can be exchanged for turn-up card before play

ante.reason: Derda does not use ante posting as a standard action.

deal.description: Dealer distributes opening packets and reveal card for trump suggestion.
deal.constraints: Dealer-only during setup before bidding and trick play.

reveal_market.reason: Derda has no market reveal mechanic.

buy_market.reason: Players do not buy cards from a market in Derda.

buy_stock.reason: Stock purchase is not part of Derda gameplay.

fold.reason: Trick-taking deals are played out; fold action is not used.

check.reason: Checking is a betting term and does not apply to Derda.

call.reason: No call action exists in Derda's bidding structure.

bet.reason: Derda scoring uses trick points and bonuses, not wagers.

raise.reason: Raise mechanics are not used in this game.

declare.reason: No separate declaration phase is used in Derda.

reveal_hand.reason: Outcome is based on trick captures and words, not full-hand reveal.

award_pot.description: Assign trick points and bonus words to update cumulative score.
award_pot.constraints: Executed after all tricks in the deal are completed.

play_card.description: Play one legal card following suit and trump obligations.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit if possible; otherwise trump when required.

draw.reason: Players do not draw as a recurring action during trick phase.

discard.reason: Discarding is not a standalone action in Derda.

pass.reason: Players must contribute a card when it is their trick turn.

bid.description: Select to play offered trump or pass into alternate contract options.
bid.constraints: Used in trump-selection stage before full trick play begins.

meld.reason: Derda does not use meld declarations in the rummy sense.

go_out.reason: Deal ends after trick completion, not via going out.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: When trump is led must play higher trump if possible; when cannot follow suit must play trump if held.

edgeCases.text: If defender scores more than declarer, defender takes all points and declarer scores nothing; defender deals next.
If players tie, defender scores their points; declarer points held for next deal winner.
Player may call enough after winning a trick when they believe they have reached 500; if correct they win, if wrong opponent wins.
If a player would reach 500 by words alone without taking a trick, the deal is replayed.

engine.handRankingSystem: Highest trump or highest led suit wins each trick under Derda order.
engine.rankingSystem: Cumulative trick points and bonus words determine first player to 500.
engine.deckDescription: A stripped French deck containing 32 cards with four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) and eight ranks per suit (7 through Ace), created by removing all 2s through 6s from a standard 52-card deck.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy recognition during gameplay.
engine.rankDescription: Eight ranks per suit in ascending order: 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack (Valet), Queen (Dame), King (Roi), and Ace as the highest card, where each rank determines card strength and eligibility for building sequences.
engine.dealPattern: Deal 6 cards each, choose trump, deal 3 more each, then play out tricks.
